written.headline: U.S. midterm elections bring voter backlash and new restrictions for AI data centers
written.summary: Democratic victories in the 2026 U.S. midterms coincided with voters passing 40 out of 41 ballot measures to restrict data center development. Newly elected Democratic governors and members of Congress are also expected to push for increased regulation of Big Tech and AI.

written.headline: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
written.summary: A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, driven by price competition and savvier customers. Token spend grew only 1.5% across August and September, compared to a 42% increase in July.

written.headline: Microsoft ends Oracle AI cloud rental as older Nvidia GPUs become obsolete
written.summary: Microsoft has stopped renewing its 2023 agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle, turning off the rented capacity in recent months. The move is attributed to Oracle’s use of older‑generation Nvidia GPUs that no longer meet Microsoft’s AI workload needs.

written.headline: Meta pauses commercial terms update that would have allowed AI training on linked sites
written.summary: Meta has indefinitely delayed planned updates to its commercial terms that would have required business account users to allow AI training on external websites linked on Facebook. The changes, originally set to take effect October 30 and later pushed to November 20, 2026, were paused after court injunctions in Brazil and Norway and a UK CMA investigation.
